PromptCacheBreakpoint.title: PromptCacheBreakpoint
PromptCacheBreakpoint.description:
Marks the end of a reusable prompt prefix (OpenAI GPT-5.6 and newer).

Set it on the last content part of the stable prefix you want cached: the prompt
up to and including that part is stored and reused on later requests that share it,
reducing latency and cost. Providers enforce a minimum token count below which
caching is skipped. Ignored by models that don't support explicit cache breakpoints.

mode.title: Mode
mode.description: "implicit" (default) caches automatically and also honors any prompt_cache_breakpoint you set; "explicit" caches only the blocks you mark with prompt_cache_breakpoint. Known values are advertised in the schema but not enforced.

ttl.title: Ttl
ttl.description: How long to keep the prompt cache, e.g. "30m". Leave unset for the provider default. Known values are advertised in the schema but not enforced.

PromptCacheOptions.title: PromptCacheOptions
PromptCacheOptions.description:
Request-level prompt-cache settings (OpenAI GPT-5.6 and newer).

Controls how this request's prompt cache behaves — whether caching happens
automatically or only on the blocks you mark with ``prompt_cache_breakpoint``, and
how long the cache is kept. Ignored by models that don't support prompt caching.

sort.title: Sort
sort.description: What to optimise for when several providers serve the requested model. 'cost' (default) picks the cheapest for this request's shape; 'speed' the highest tokens/second; 'latency' the fastest to first token; 'exact' the most reliable at producing well-formed tool calls / structured output. Health is always a filter first — no mode will route you to a failing provider. Can also be written as a model suffix, e.g. 'gpt-5.5:speed'.

sticky.title: Sticky
sticky.description: Keep a conversation on the provider holding its prompt cache. On by default, and only ever active for models whose providers discount cache reads. Set false to route every request independently on price instead. Naming an explicit `sort` or an `order` also takes priority over cache affinity.

allow_fallbacks.title: Allow Fallbacks
allow_fallbacks.description: Whether other providers of the same model may be tried when the chosen one fails. On by default. Set false to pin the request to the single best provider: it then fails rather than silently moving to another seller, useful when a cache-warm prompt would cold-miss elsewhere. This governs PROVIDERS of the requested model only; models you list in `fallbacks` are your own choice and are always kept.

quality_cost.title: Quality Cost
quality_cost.description: Only with model='@edenai': how far to trade answer quality for cost when the platform chooses the MODEL. 0 asks for the best model for the request, 10 for the cheapest model that can still handle it, values in between blend the two; omit it to leave the choice to the platform (quality first). This is the one `routing` field that steers the model rather than the provider — `sort` never changes which model is chosen.

allowed_providers.title: Allowed Providers
allowed_providers.description: Restrict routing to these providers, e.g. ['openai', 'anthropic']. Only providers that serve the requested model are considered, so an entry that does not sell it is simply inert. If none of them do, the request fails rather than falling back to a provider you excluded. Case-insensitive. Applies to routed providers only. a concrete 'provider/model' you named in `fallbacks` is your own choice and is kept.

zero_data_retention.title: Zero Data Retention
zero_data_retention.description: Serve this request only from providers that keep no prompts or outputs, and save neither its content nor its response. Applies to every model in the request, including a concrete 'provider/model' and your `fallbacks`: one that is not zero data retention fails the request. It can only add the restriction. When your organization requires zero data retention, `false` does not lift it.

ignored_providers.title: Ignored Providers
ignored_providers.description: Never route to these providers, e.g. ['deepinfra']. The mirror of `allowed_providers`: an entry that does not sell the requested model is inert, and if the list removes every seller the request fails rather than falling back to one you excluded. Case-insensitive. A provider named in both lists is a validation error. A concrete 'provider/model' you named in `fallbacks` is your own choice and is kept.

order.title: Order
order.description: Providers to try first, in this order, e.g. ['azure', 'openai']. They become the head of the fallback chain; the remaining providers of the model follow, ranked by `sort` (or load-balanced on price when no `sort` is given). An entry that does not sell the model is inert. A provider our health data marks as down is moved to the end of the chain whatever its position here. Naming an `order` turns cache affinity off, as naming a `sort` does. Case-insensitive.

max_price.description: Only route to providers whose listed per-token rates are at or under this price, in USD per MILLION tokens, e.g. {'input': 2.5, 'output': 10}. Either side may be omitted. Providers priced by another unit (per image, per second) are unaffected. If no provider of the model is within the ceiling the request fails and names the cheapest one.

ProviderRoutingPreferences.title: ProviderRoutingPreferences
ProviderRoutingPreferences.description:
How to choose between SELLERS of one model — and, with ``@edenai``, how far to trade
quality for cost when the platform chooses the model. ``order``, ``allowed_providers``,
``ignored_providers`` and ``max_price`` shape WHICH sellers and in what order; ``sort``
ranks the rest.

The seller fields are only meaningful when `model` is a canonical name (`gpt-5.5`) rather than a concrete
`provider/model` — with a concrete id there is nothing to choose between. For choosing the
MODEL itself see ``router_candidates`` and ``model="@edenai"``, which is a different router;
``quality_cost`` below is the one field here that speaks to it.

RefusalAnswer.title: RefusalAnswer
RefusalAnswer.description:
The provider declined this one question without saying why; the other answers still
stand. OpenAI's Decisions API returns these, TypeSafe's format has no equivalent.

tags.description: Up to 10 key/value labels recorded with this call, for filtering and grouping usage. Merged with the `X-EdenAI-Tags` header.

routing.description: How to pick between the providers that serve the requested model. Applies when `model` is a model name with no provider prefix (e.g. 'gpt-5.5'); ignored for a concrete 'provider/model' id, which already names its provider, except `zero_data_retention`, which holds every model in the request to it. With model='@edenai' the platform chooses the model too: `quality_cost` steers that choice, and the provider fields apply whenever the chosen model is a provider-less name.

fallbacks.title: Fallbacks
fallbacks.description: List of fallback model IDs to try if the primary model fails. Models are tried in order. Example: ['anthropic/claude-3-opus', 'openai/gpt-4o']

session_id.title: Session Id
session_id.description: Identifies a conversation, so its requests keep reaching the provider that holds its prompt cache. Any stable string you choose — a thread id, a ticket number, an agent run. Also accepted as the `x-session-id` header, for clients that cannot add body fields, and read from the headers coding agents already send (`x-claude-code-session-id`, `x-session-affinity`, `session-id`, `session_id`, `x-client-request-id`); the body field wins if both are sent. Without one, a conversation is recognised from its opening messages instead.

router_candidates.title: Router Candidates
router_candidates.description: Models the '@edenai' router may choose BETWEEN — it picks the model, whereas `routing` picks the provider for a model you already named. Used only when model='@edenai'. Each entry is a bare model name (e.g. 'gpt-5.5' — the winner's provider is then picked like any provider-less request) or a 'provider/model' id (e.g. 'openai/gpt-5-nano' — the winner is served by that exact provider). Entries the router cannot rank are skipped and listed under `edenai_metadata.routing.auto.dropped`; entries naming a model already in the list collapse into its earliest spelling, which decides how the winner is returned. The request fails only when no entry is left. If not provided, the router chooses from a default pool of eligible catalog models. At most 64 entries of up to 128 characters each.

pre_hooks.title: Pre Hooks
pre_hooks.description: List of hooks to run before the LLM provider call. Each entry must have an 'action' key and optional 'params'. Example: [{'action': 'pdf_text_extract', 'params': {'method': 'default'}}]

post_hooks.title: Post Hooks
post_hooks.description: List of hooks to run after the LLM provider call. Each entry must have an 'action' key and optional 'params'. Example: [{'action': 'json_heal', 'params': {'json_schema': {...}}}]

input.title: Input
input.description: Text, image, or file inputs to the model. Optional when continuing a conversation via previous_response_id.

instructions.title: Instructions
instructions.description: System/developer instructions prepended to input. Not carried over when using previous_response_id.

previous_response_id.title: Previous Response Id
previous_response_id.description: ID of a prior response to continue a multi-turn conversation. The provider manages conversation state server-side.

stream.title: Stream
stream.description: Whether to stream the response via server-sent events.

tools.title: Tools
tools.description: List of tools the model may call (function, web_search, file_search, etc.).

tool_choice.title: Tool Choice
tool_choice.description: Controls which tool is called. 'auto', 'required', 'none', or a specific tool object.

truncation.title: Truncation
truncation.description: How to handle context that exceeds the model's context window.

store.title: Store
store.description: Whether the provider should store the response server-side for later retrieval.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Up to 16 key-value pairs for tagging.

user.title: User
user.description: Stable end-user identifier for abuse detection.

prompt_cache_key.title: Prompt Cache Key
prompt_cache_key.description: Prompt-cache routing hint (OpenAI): requests sharing a key and a common prompt prefix are routed to the same cache shard, improving hit rates for high-volume shared prefixes. Forwarded to providers that support it, dropped elsewhere. Also read for provider stickiness when no `session_id` or session header is given.

prompt_cache_retention.title: Prompt Cache Retention
prompt_cache_retention.description: How long the provider retains the prompt cache — OpenAI currently accepts "in_memory" (provider default, typically 5-10 minutes) and "24h" (extended retention, supported on gpt-5.x and gpt-4.1). The known values are advertised in the schema but not enforced: the value is passed through verbatim for the provider to validate, so new provider values work without an Eden AI release. Dropped for providers that don't support it.

prompt_cache_options.description: Request-level prompt-cache settings (mode and ttl) for OpenAI GPT-5.6 and newer models. Ignored by models that don't support prompt caching.

include.title: Include
include.description: Additional output data to include, e.g. 'file_search_call.results'.

background.title: Background
background.description: Whether to run the model response in the background.

service_tier.title: Service Tier
service_tier.description: Processing tier, billed at that tier's rates (e.g. 'ultrafast' on openai/gpt-6.1-sol and openai/gpt-6-astra). A model that has no rates for the requested priority or ultrafast tier runs on the default tier; the response's service_tier reports the tier that ran.

id.title: Id
id.description: Provider id to pass as `model` or in the path.

zero_data_retention.description: true when calls to this entry keep no prompts or outputs after the response (Zero Data Retention), under Eden AI's terms with its provider: the model's own terms when they differ, else the provider's; a customer-hosted model is always true. false when they are kept, null when not verified yet.

provider_params.title: Provider Params
provider_params.description: The `provider_params` each provider accepts, for subfeatures that restrict them; any other parameter is rejected with 400. Each entry is a parameter path in the provider's own request format, nested keys joined with dots (e.g. `videogenerationconfig.seed`), matched case-insensitively: send the keys in the provider's own casing (`{"videoGenerationConfig": {"seed": 7}}`). An empty list means the provider accepts none; `null` on subfeatures that publish no list.
